svg.title: TTN IR Model Architecture
svg.desc: Focused model architecture diagram for the Tree Tensor Network IR classifier implemented in model.py.
svg.text: Focused architecture view for [`src/spectroscopy_qml/ir/tree_tensor_network/model.py`] with an explicit binary reduction tree
FROM RAW IR SPECTRUM TO LEAF STATES
each sample is one interpolated IR spectrum
first 8 segments have length 57, remaining 24 have length 56
scale by `x_max`, then map each scalar to
output shape `(batch, 32, 57, 2)` using padded max length 57
mask padded values, flatten each segment,
apply one linear projection and normalize
32 leaf vectors enter the binary TTN
each leaf is a normalized state of size `chi`
this is the exact tensor interface consumed by `TensorMerge`
The model builds a strict binary reduction tree because `num_segments` must be a power of two.
At each level, adjacent node pairs are contracted by one shared `TensorMerge(chi, chi, chi)` module for that level.
Each merge renormalizes the output, keeping the TTN state stable across repeated contractions.
leaf tensor shape: `(batch, chi)` per segment
single root state used by output head
returns logits, optional sigmoid in forward()
the tree is the core architectural idea
all other blocks prepare or consume tree states
flatten + linear projection to bond dimension `chi`
learnable rank-3 tensor contraction `(..., chi) x (..., chi)`
orchestrates segmentation, tree reduction, and final logits
`num_segments` must be a power of two
all node states live in the same bond dimension `chi`

The TTN model does not use a generic dense stack as its main encoder. It converts spectrum segments into local states and then reduces them through an explicit binary tensor tree until one root representation remains.
